long_biography.plain_text:
Walter Graeme Ladd's most durable achievement was the Kate Macy Ladd Fund, created under his will to continue the convalescent care his wife had begun at their Natirar estate. The bequest preserved a practical philanthropic priority after the couple's earlier plan for a joint Macy–Ladd foundation gave way to differing interests in convalescence and medical science.

Born in 1856 and raised in an upper-middle-class Brooklyn household, Ladd recorded his occupation as merchant when he married Kate Macy in 1883. Her inherited fortune derived from a family shipping concern that entered oil refining and was later acquired by Standard Oil. Ladd eventually gave up outside business, devoting himself to his frequently ill wife's care and to managing their investments and estates in New Jersey and Maine.
